My daughter,

1. I cannot understand how you have not received my letters telling you to send Sr. A. Guglielma to Foligno; the one from Foligno, Sr. A. Berarda, will come to you and you will leave her as superior;1 and when that is done you will come and spend the feast days here with me, for after Christmas you must set out again to open a House, and you will be happy.2

She has received two letters after two months. She repeats that the Novices and one or two Sisters must be sent to Italy. The circular letter is being written; she will do her best to get it to her. She speaks of the Cardinal Protector. She urges her to help financially, pointing out that she has not paid for the cloth bought for her. Let her decide once and for all.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

1. I have just received your two letters; in one you say you do not receive mine, but I must tell you I have been very anxious, for it is two months since I had any; I have always written except in October.1 I admit this because I had bad bronchitis, but I am better now, just convalescing a little.

2. I cannot understand how you never receive my letters, in which I always repeat the same things: send me Sr. A. Clelia with the 3 Novices, and I would send you others. You could also send Sr. A. Annunciata, and they could bring me everything, for it is now three years, and certainly, if you saw how things are here!2 Enough. You can understand me if you will. You say the sisters have more or less rebelled, but what came over them? Anyway, from the last letter I see they are calm. May God keep them in peace and make them always persevere.3 You do well to keep watch.

3. I am registering this one and addressing it to the Bishop so that you can have it. No — for fear of loss I will send it to you instead; indeed I nearly always register them, but still I worry; a friar has offered, saying he has a way of getting them to you safely. The circular is now being prepared, so we will send you two, and I will make a packet of it and send it to your Bishop, who will give it to you.4

4. You received my letter enclosing a copy you were to make and send to the Cardinal Protector, Cardinal Alimonda.5 He came here to the Mother House and took possession. What a fine ceremony! He is the first, for the others could not take possession, as we were not then approved; but now he has been appointed by papal decree.6 He has visited several Houses and will soon go to the one in Naples too.

5. As for the fur you say you wanted to send the Bishop of Piacenza, do not send it to him but to the Cardinal;7 but when? If you keep everything and never send anything? What are you keeping it all for? You make me laugh. For three years you have been promising, but I see nothing. Poor Italians, if we had to wait for something from you, poor me! Instead I always have to toil terribly and rack my brains to keep so many people! God's will be done!

6. Listen, I sent you the cloth and it did arrive.8 If I had always done as you do and waited, what would you have said? Ah! how many complaints, because it did not reach you quickly; and yet that little cost me nearly 2000 — can you imagine? You do not believe it, but I can send you the merchant's list and you will see how dear these goods have become. But there it is: I had to pay the bill, for the merchant would not wait.9 That too came out of these four old bones.

7. So send whichever sister you think fit with the two or three novices, Sr. A. Clelia, and Sr. A. Amadio, who I hear is not too [well]. It seems to me you can quite well do it, for the number is kept up by the others you have clothed, isn't it?10 So you must get moving now, otherwise! We never reach a [conclusion].

8. I hope at last to hear something definite, for your letters are always the same, always saying the same things, and nothing is ever settled. You know, I am a practical woman, and that is how I like the Daughters of Saint Anne to be.

9. And tell Sr. A. Cunegonda I will write to her with the others.11 I am so busy! However, I have written to all of them and hope you have received all the letters; with greetings to you all, believe me yours and your affectionate M. ROSA
